text: A clear explanation of the project, experiments, and actual results
Faculty presentation • Evidence from the completed simulator experiments
Opening: PRESTO-R is a research prototype for choosing network routes. Evidence comes from this project simulator, not a production network. Sources: README.md; results/report.md.
A route may become slow, crowded, or unavailable while data is travelling.
A reactive router waits for visible trouble, then changes route.
A predictive router may leave early, but can change routes too often.
The project tests whether prediction plus a switching cost balances delivery and stability.
Route flapping means switching back and forth too frequently.

Use a delivery-van analogy: choose among four roads. PRESTO-R tries to use warning clues without overreacting. This is the project motivation, not a universal claim about every routing system. Source: results/report.md sections 1–2.
One managed flow plus background traffic.
Python fluid simulator; synthetic congestion and failures.
GRU risk predictor + DQN route choice + switch penalty.
NSFNET and generated RGG; five scenarios.
OUT OF SCOPE OR NOT COMPLETED
Production deployment or real traffic validation.

Fluid means traffic rates rather than individual packets. Failures are synthetic and may include designed precursors. Missing ablation is no-prediction plus switch penalty (reactive_dqn_pen). Sources: results/report.md sections 2,6; Phase 7 plan.

text: Each circle is a router/node; each line is a link. The graph layout is for readability, not geography. Exact node pairs are listed in presto/sim/topology.py as NSFNET_EDGES. Source: presto/sim/topology.py.
A benchmark-style topology, not a live network being simulated.
The code builds 14 numbered nodes and 21 fixed undirected links.
NSFNET is the primary experiment topology; RGG is the second map.
The project creates its own traffic, link delays, and failure events.

NSFNET historically names a U.S. research network. This project uses a standard graph topology as a repeatable benchmark-style test map; it does not recreate historical traffic or operations. Sources: configs/topo/nsfnet.yaml; results/report.md T1.
The same loop repeats each simulation tick.

Simulator advances; agent gets telemetry and path features; predictor emits risk; DQN chooses an integer path action; reward is returned for learning. Future schedule and true link health are hidden from learned agents. Sources: presto-r-plan/00_overview.md; results/report.md T1.
Phases 0–6 form the core; Phase 7 is optional.
After Phase 1, predictor and baseline work can proceed in parallel.
Each phase adds a component needed by the next one.
Phase 7 would use packet-level NS-3, but its checks remain incomplete.
Roadmap from presto-r-plan/00_overview.md and README. Phases 0–6 are the core; optional Phase 7 is not in final results.

text: Standard W=10, H=5. Bad link if down, true loss >.05, or true delay >3× base delay. Final held-out overall onset F1=.5296; precursor-only subgroup=.7476. All-sample metrics are easier because already-bad links are included. Sources: results/report.md T2; results/success_criteria.md; presto/predictor/gru.py.
Baselines help isolate what prediction and the switch penalty contribute.

DQN = Deep Q-Network. Stable-Baselines3 supplies DQN, trained by presto/agents/train.py. Oracle sees future schedule and is not deployable. The reactive policy is an internal inspired baseline, not a full external RQSMR reproduction. Sources: phase-3 and phase-4 plans.
It tells the agent which trade-offs matter.
PRESTO-R λ = 0.5 → each route change costs 0.5 reward points
Too little: route flapping. Too much: may stay on a failing path.

Formula from presto/reward.py. Standard α=1, β=4, γ=0, μ=.05; PRESTO λ=.5. D normalized delay; L loss; T delivered/demand; S switch indicator; E normalized hops. With γ=0 there is no separate throughput bonus. λ selected on validation.
Checks cover components, learned behavior, and final comparisons.
Unit/integration checks: topology, simulator, failures, telemetry, state, reward, environment.
Predictor checks: split leakage, output shape, save/load, held-out metrics.
Policy checks: heuristic choices, deterministic rollouts, training smoke, risk-use diagnostic.
Experiment checks: held-out grid, paired statistics, robustness, rerun hashes.
Release checkpoint records 74 tests; a later Phase 5 note records 97 tests.
Counts 74 and 97 refer to different checkpoints, not one combined run. Repository test files are under tests/. Sources: README; phase-5 and phase-6 plans.
Methods see the same scenarios for fair paired comparisons.
2 topologies × 5 scenarios × 200 held-out seeds per scenario/topology.
Test seeds 10000–10199; λ tuned on validation, not test data.
5 training seeds for learned NSFNET agents; 3 for RGG agents.
38,400 episode-metric rows; Wilcoxon tests with Holm correction.
Also tested horizons H=3/H=10, 2× noise, +50% load, and sudden failures.
Seeds match across methods for paired testing. Across-training-seed standard deviation describes learned-agent variation. Sources: results/report.md; README.md; configs/grid/main.yaml.

title: Main result — fewer switches, similar delivery

text: Main result — fewer switches, similar delivery
75.2% fewer switches than Predictive DQN; PDR difference +0.0017.

alt: Main held-out NSFNET results by scenario

text: Exact values: report.md T3, mixed NSFNET. Reduction (20.988−5.197)/20.988 ≈75.2%. PDR difference .0017 = .17 percentage points. Phrase conclusion as a simulator result.
The final report includes passes and failures.

Source results/success_criteria.md. PRESTO did not meet the predeclared significant PDR-and-recovery comparison to reactive on failure cases. Slightly higher average PDR does not satisfy the full criterion.
This is evidence about the simulator, not proof about real networks.
Fluid model: no individual packet timing or full protocol behavior.
One managed flow; synthetic failures and designed precursor patterns.
Predictor trained on simulator telemetry may face distribution shift.
No-prediction + switch-penalty ablation was not run.
NS-3 packet validation and real traffic traces remain future work.
Takeaway: clear stability benefit, with important prediction and recovery limits.
Sources: results/report.md discussion; Phase 7 optional plan. Suggested next steps: improve onset prediction, finish the missing ablation, and validate with NS-3 and real traces.
